llm.summary: This is a local healthcare table-checking skill with no network use, persistence, or hidden data movement found, but users should minimize sensitive patient data in inputs.

dimensions.detail: The skill processes healthcare, billing, inventory, and device traceability tables, which may contain sensitive data; this is purpose-aligned and local-only, but the skill should more explicitly tell users to de-identify PHI/PII.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install hooks, package managers, external dependencies, or remote payload retrieval were found; use is via the documented local Node script.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The manifest includes some broad Chinese keywords, but runtime routing scores the pasted table header, refuses no-match or tied matches, and does not include prompt overrides or hidden agent-control instructions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, credential access, environment-variable use, writes, background workers, or network calls were found; file reads are limited to packaged files and user-specified input paths.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is healthcare and medical-supply reconciliation across 8 subskills, and the package contains a manifest plus local engines for all 8 with scoped checks and out-of-scope disclaimers.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Use this for local reconciliation of exported healthcare tables, not as a medical, legal, billing, or regulatory certification. De-identify or minimize patient, staff, supplier, and account data before pasting whenever possible, and have qualified staff review any compliance or financial conclusions.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The broad 8-subskill claim is supported by artifact evidence: the manifest lists 8 subskills, all 8 engine files are present, and run.mjs lists and routes among them, so the claimed single-skill mismatch was not validated.
[SQP-2] expected: Pasting healthcare tables is central to the skill, and execution is local with no writes or network use; the missing PHI/PII minimization warning is a user-guidance issue rather than a Review-level security concern.
[AE1] unexpected: The referenced scripts/run.mjs file was present and inspected; it is a local CLI dispatcher and not an analysis-evasion gap.
[LP1] unexpected: No process.env or environment-secret access was found in the inspected code; the apparent env concern is not supported by the artifact.
[SQP-1] expected: Generic routing keywords exist in the manifest, but the actual dispatcher relies on table-header matching and refuses ambiguous or unmatched inputs, reducing unintended processing risk.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-only labels and descriptions are consistent with the skill's Chinese presentation and are not evidence of hidden or unsafe behavior.
[A.I.G SARIF] expected: The static scan reported no results, which is consistent with the inspected local deterministic implementation.
